Class TTLLFormatterBuilder

java.lang.Object
io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.TTLLFormatterBuilder
All Implemented Interfaces:
LogBuilder<TTLLFormatterBuilder, LogFormatter>
public final class TTLLFormatterBuilder extends Object implements LogBuilder<TTLLFormatterBuilder, LogFormatter>
Builder to create LogFormatter. The TTLL (Time, Thread, Level, Logger) text format, the default encoder, with each part configurable, see TTLL.

The defaults produce 12:00:00.123 [main] INFO com.example.App - hello followed by any stack trace. Parts set to none are left out along with their separating space. As properties of the encoder, each part is one of the lowercase names of its TTLL enum, for example logging.appender.console.encoder.ttll.keyValues=json5; keyValues accepts json and json5 as well as true (percent encoding) and false (none). The timestamp property also accepts a DateTimeFormatter pattern in UTC. The color property decides whether to color and the theme property which colors; when neither is set the rainbowgum theme is used if the console supports ANSI.

Property Pattern Type Required Default Description
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.timestamp String (converted) true ttll Time formatter, see TTLL.TimestampFormat.
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.thread String (converted) true name Thread formatter in square brackets, see TTLL.ThreadFormat.
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.level String (converted) true padded Level formatter, see TTLL.LevelFormat.
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.logger String (converted) true full Logger name formatter, see TTLL.LoggerFormat.
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.keyValues String (converted) true percent Key values formatter in braces, see TTLL.KeyValuesFormat.
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.color String (converted) false null Whether to color, see TTLL.ColorMode.
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.theme String (converted) false null ANSI color theme, see TTLL.ColorTheme.
logging.appender.{name}.encoder.ttll.keyValuesWhenEmpty String (converted) false null Braces for no key values, see TTLL.KeyValuesWhenEmpty.
